units: Defines empirical conditions under which Adaptive Inheritance would be considered unsupported.
Framework's narrow claim is persistent unblocked contradiction should produce measurable authority redistribution away from invalid mechanisms.
FT-001: Adaptive Inheritance Criterion / Claim and criteria
ARR<1 after persistent unambiguous contradiction; failure if ARR approximately 1 while LBR tends to 1.
FT-002: Confidence/Authority Separation / Claim and criteria
Confidence and authority need not covary perfectly; failure condition proposes near-perfect inverse correlation across tested agents.
FT-003: MRAT Parsimony / Claim and criteria
Lowest-cost intervention should be sufficient; failure includes REE on noise or generator rewrite when mechanism update suffices.
FT-004: REE Necessity Condition / Claim and criteria
Expansion requires local saturation and positive future gain; failure if expansion occurs with nonpositive net adaptive value.
FT-005: ADI Validity / Claim and criteria
High ADI should predict higher ARR and longer latency; failure if correlation between ADI and ARR is approximately zero.
FT-006: ARR Validity / Claim and criteria
Known decoupled systems should have ARR toward 1 and known corrigible systems toward 0; reversed behavior falsifies metric validity.
FT-007: Capability Independence / Claim and criteria
Corrigibility should not collapse into static capability; failure if accuracy and ACS correlate approximately 1.
FT-008: Adaptive Latency Constraint / Claim and criteria
Delayed correction should relate to inheritance persistence; failure if correlation between tau_adapt and ARR is zero.
Every evaluation suite should include non-structural contradictions to distinguish adaptation from instability and overreaction.
Noise control uses y=3x+epsilon and expects attribution to Noise.
True structural failure is expected to route to Mechanism, Representation, or Generator.
Support requires healthy agents to have lower ARR and latency, higher ACS, and better parsimony than failed/gratuitous controls.

Checklist requires metric predictions, negative controls, REE justification records, structural distance, ARR, latency, separated capability tests, and pre-optimization failure documentation; all items are unchecked.
If empirical evidence fails to support Reality -> Authority Redistribution -> Future Adaptation, framework should be revised or abandoned.
Terms 'persistent', 'unambiguous', and ARR approximately 1 lack numerical decision thresholds and sampling rules.
Correlation thresholds are heuristic and no sample size, uncertainty, multiple-testing, or causal-identification procedure is specified.
The source invokes 'known decoupled' and 'known corrigible' systems without defining an independent gold standard.
No complete benchmark population, statistical decision rule, or preregistered acceptance threshold is specified.
The unchecked checklist is a prospective release requirement, not evidence that validation has occurred.
